FRA.note: World's largest live-cattle exporter by liveweight; values are LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT also reports head-count, but this dataset uses the tonnage basis). France shipped ~1.47 million head in 2024, mostly young 'broutards'/feeder cattle to Italy (64%) and Spain (24%) for fattening (INTERBEV/FAOSTAT 2024). Combined cattle+sheep+goat+pig basket, dominated by cattle HS0102.

DNK.note: Europe's largest live-pig (weaner/piglet) exporter; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES basis. ~14 million weaners shipped in 2024 to Germany and Poland for finishing (FAOSTAT/Danish Agriculture & Food Council 2024). Almost entirely swine HS0103.

NLD.note: Major intra-EU live-animal trade and transit hub (weaner pigs, calves, breeding stock); LIVEWEIGHT TONNES. Large two-way flows with Germany, Belgium, Spain, Italy (FAOSTAT 2024). Cattle+pig basket.

AUS.note: World's leading long-haul live exporter; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES. 2024 live cattle 766,044 head (Indonesia ~70%, Vietnam 16%, China 7%) plus 433,078 live sheep (Jordan now top market) per MLA State of the Industry 2024. Live sheep-by-sea is being phased out by law from May 2028.

DEU.note: Large two-way trader: net importer of Danish/Dutch weaner pigs for finishing, also exports calves and breeding stock; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT 2024). Mixed cattle+pig basket.

ESP.note: Major fattening hub importing French/Dutch feeder cattle and exporting live cattle/sheep to Portugal and to North Africa & the Middle East (Libya, Lebanon, Algeria); LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT 2024).

CAN.note: Large live-cattle and feeder-pig exporter to the United States (integrated North American market); LIVEWEIGHT TONNES. Roughly 0.6-0.7 million live cattle plus several million weaner/feeder pigs cross to the US annually (USDA/Statistics Canada 2024).

MEX.note: Largest single supplier of feeder cattle to US feedlots (~1.0-1.2 million head in 2024, periodically disrupted by New World screwworm border closures); LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (USDA GATS 2024). Cattle HS0102.

BRA.note: Long-haul live-cattle exporter by sea to Turkey, Egypt, Iraq and Lebanon; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT 2024). Contentious domestically on welfare grounds, with periodic court challenges to the trade.

SDN.note: Historic top supplier of live sheep to Saudi Arabia across the Red Sea; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES. Civil war from 2023 has disrupted exports and ceded share to Somalia (FAOSTAT 2024). Mostly sheep+goat HS0104.

SOM.note: Major Horn-of-Africa live sheep/goat/camel exporter via Berbera and Bosaso to Saudi Arabia and the Gulf; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES. Exports surged in 2024 as Sudan retreated (FAOSTAT/Saudi MEWA 2024). Sheep+goat HS0104.

URY.note: South American live-cattle exporter by sea to Turkey and the eastern Mediterranean; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT 2024). Cattle HS0102.

IDN.note: World's largest live-cattle importer, taking ~70% of Australia's live cattle for feedlot finishing near consumption centres; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT/MLA 2024). Cattle HS0102.

ITA.note: Largest EU live-cattle importer; fattens French/eastern-European feeder cattle in Po Valley feedlots; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT 2024). Cattle HS0102 dominates the basket.

SAU.note: World's largest live-sheep importer; Ramadan/Hajj/Eid demand drew >4 million sheep, cattle and camels in 2024 from Sudan, Somalia, Djibouti, Jordan, Australia, Romania and Brazil; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT/Saudi MEWA 2024).

POL.note: Major importer of Danish weaner pigs for finishing into Europe's growing pork sector; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT 2024). Swine HS0103 dominated.

CHN.note: Importer of live breeding/dairy cattle (Australia, Uruguay, Chile, NZ) and breeding pigs to upgrade herd genetics; LIVEWEIGHT TONNES (FAOSTAT 2024). Cattle+swine basket.

rankings.note: Live animals for slaughter/breeding (cattle HS0102 + swine HS0103 + sheep/goat HS0104), LIVEWEIGHT TONNES basis (FAOSTAT also publishes head-count). Rankings from FAOSTAT 2024 trade balances, cross-checked against UN Comtrade 2024 and MLA/USDA: France leads on feeder cattle, Denmark/Netherlands on weaner pigs, Australia on long-haul cattle/sheep. Importer side led by Italy and Germany (finishing) plus Saudi Arabia (sheep).

companies.name: DanBred
companies.note: Leading global pig-genetics company (breeding stock and semen) underpinning the Danish weaner-export model; ships breeding animals across Europe and worldwide (DanBred 2024).
companies.improve: Should add head/doses exported by region and clarify live-breeding-stock vs genetics-only volumes; long-distance transport of breeding pigs raises welfare scrutiny.

companies.name: Topigs Norsvin
companies.note: One of the world's largest swine-genetics companies, supplying breeding gilts and boars across the EU live-pig finishing network (Topigs Norsvin 2024).
companies.improve: Should quantify live breeding-stock exports vs AI/genetics and add destination split; welfare risk concentrated in long-haul breeder movements.

companies.name: Wellard
companies.note: One of Australia's largest live-cattle exporters and ship operators (purpose-built livestock vessels) serving Indonesia, Vietnam and China (Wellard 2024).
companies.improve: Should add head exported and route mix; long-haul sea transport of cattle is the central animal-welfare flashpoint for the sector.

companies.name: Australian Rural Exports (Austrex)
companies.note: Long-established Australian live exporter of slaughter, feeder and breeder cattle and (historically) sheep to Asia and the Middle East (Austrex 2024).
companies.improve: Should disclose volumes by species/market; exposed to Australia's legislated phase-out of live sheep by sea from May 2028.

companies.name: Charolais France / GIE France Genetique Elevage
companies.note: French beef-breeding and feeder-cattle export network channeling 'broutards' and breeding stock to Italy, Spain and third countries (France Genetique Elevage 2024).
companies.improve: Should separate breeding-stock from feeder-cattle volumes; intra-EU calf transport durations are a recurring welfare concern.

companies.name: Livestock Transport & Trading Co. (Saudi/Gulf importers)
companies.note: Representative Gulf live-sheep import channel aggregating Sudanese, Somali, Australian and Romanian stock for Hajj/Eid demand (FAOSTAT/Saudi MEWA 2024); specific importer named generically as the trade is fragmented.
companies.improve: Should be replaced with a named, sourced importer once company-level Saudi import data is available; flagged modeled because the entity is representative, not a single verified firm.

global.note: World live-animal trade (cattle HS0102 + swine HS0103 + sheep/goat HS0104), LIVEWEIGHT TONNES exported (FAOSTAT 2024). 'Production'/'consumption' are not meaningful for live trade (animals are an input to meat/dairy, not a final commodity), so only the traded volume is series-tracked; roughly 8.5-9 Mt liveweight crosses borders annually, dominated by intra-EU weaner-pig and feeder-cattle flows plus long-haul cattle to Asia and sheep to the Gulf.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2025-2034 envelope applied to traded liveweight; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6
